meta.title: Ride Fleet — one operations spine for your whole fleet
meta.description: Rental and dealership loaners on one operations spine, with AutoExpreso and SunPass tolls reconciled and AI customer service in Spanish and English. Built in Puerto Rico, ready for the US mainland.

hero.lede: Traditional rental and dealership loaners — with tolls and AI customer service — on one operations spine. From booking to closeout, without jumping between systems.

spec.label: Language
spec.value: Spanish and English, native — not translated

app.ariaLabel: Ride Fleet Manager dashboard: today's turns, 128 units across three rooftops, turn-ready score, utilization and reconciled tolls.

callouts.body: Every point traces to wash, damage or fuel.

callouts.body: Every unit knows what's next: wash, handoff or shop.

router.title: What's bleeding money right now?
router.aside: Pick the leak that hurts most. Each door leads to the product that closes it — and all three run on the same base, so you start with one and expand once it pays for itself.

doors.title: Tolls you never billed
doors.sub: The toll posts weeks later, nobody remembers who was driving, and the house eats it.
doors.verbSub: Toll Bridge collects from AutoExpreso and SunPass, matches every crossing to the booking that caused it, and bills it.

doors.title: Calls nobody answers after 5
doors.sub: The customer doesn't leave a message — they call the next shop. The rental you lost doesn't show up in any report.

total.label: The shop next door got it

doors.verbSub: Every call answered, in Spanish or English, around the clock — with a human team behind it for what shouldn't be decided alone.

doors.title: A different system for every business model
doors.sub: Rental in one tool, loaners in a spreadsheet. Closing the month is a full-time job.
doors.verbSub: Rental and loaners on one engine, with modules and permissions per rooftop.

spine.title: One record. Three products.
spine.aside: Toll Bridge and Voz AI don't "integrate" with Ride Fleet Manager — they write to the same booking, the same customer and the same vehicle.

events.text: Call answered in Spanish. Booking created in the conversation.
Unit HTR·142 assigned — turn-ready 96, available at SJU.
Agreement signed and check-out inspection with 12 photos.
AutoExpreso crossing $1.75 matched to this booking.
Return and check-in inspection. No new damage.
$5.25 in tolls added to the booking closeout.
Receipt sent by SMS plus confirmation of the next rental.

toggle.strong: Start with one leak. Expand when it pays for itself.
toggle.rest: Turning on the next module is a setting, not an integration project: no migration, no double entry, no file someone has to upload every night.

score.foot: Every point traces to a timestamped, photographed event.

list.body: Shortage, maintenance, wash and priority are configured per account and per rooftop. The planner proposes moves that respect that operation's rules, not an industry average.
A copilot that proposes the day's plan and explains why it moves each unit — in the language you work in.
No unit is "ready" just because. The breakdown on the left is the real screen: every point deducted has an event, a timestamp and a photo behind it.

list.value: Inspections with evidence and damage triage
list.body: Check-out and check-in photos, a side-by-side compare packet and a next-best action for every damage item. The claims workspace is built on that same evidence, inside the system.
The planner takes mileage, fuel and location from Zubie and VoltSwitch. That data arrives on its own — nobody types it in or waits for the next inspection.
Spanish and English throughout — the employee app, the customer portal and the phone call. Puerto Rico first, ready for the US mainland.

cta.title: See all three on one record
cta.body: Half an hour, live, with your business model on screen — rental or loaners. No generic slide deck.
